newsitem.title: FRANCE: Basque guerrilla leaders go on trial in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Basque guerrilla leaders go on trial in Paris.

text.p: Three leaders of the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA went on trial in Paris on Tuesday, facing up to 10 years in prison on terrorism charges.
They were among some 30 French and Spanish nationals suspected of being separatist activists or sympathisers, many of whom were tried in their absence.

The three main accused were Spanish citizens. One of them, Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia, 43, was among the most wanted men in Spain, where he is accused of sending a booby-trapped car to Madrid in 1991.

Spanish police regarded him as the operational chief of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), a group which has killed some 800 people in Spain in a three-decade-long campaign for a separate Basque state.

Also on trial was Jose Luis "Txelis" Alvarez Santa Cristina, 42, believed to have been ETA's ideologist and financier, in charge of extorting "revolutionary taxes" from businessmen in the Spanish Basque country.
The third main defendant, 50-year-old Jose Maria "Fiti" Arregui Erostarbe, is said to be the group's expert on explosives and forged identity documents.
He is wanted in Spain in connection with a parcel bomb which badly maimed Fernando de Mateo Lage, presiding judge of the Audiencia Nacional anti-terrorist court, in 1990.
Several dozen sympathisers demonstrated outside the heavily-guarded law courts as the defendants arrived in police vans.
The trial opened with the questioning of five French people suspected of harbouring ETA leaders and activists. All said they were not aware their guests were guerrillas.
One of the five, Pierre Fagant, also said he was not aware ETA was running a clandestine arms workshop near his home producing hundreds of sub-machineguns a year.
If convicted, the three leaders will serve their sentences in France before being extradited to Spain.

All three were captured five years ago in a villa in the French Basque resort of Bidart by police investigating ETA's "French commando", a group blamed in Spain for bomb attacks which cost dozens of lives.
The group was broken up as it prepared a bomb attack against a government building in the southern Spanish town of Seville before the 1992 World Fair.
Seven further suspected members of the group go on trial on May 26 in a special Paris anti-terrorist court.

In a separate case, a suspected French Basque guerrilla, Jean-Noel Garispe, went on trial in a Paris anti-terrorism court in connection with four bomb attacks against two army barracks, a branch of Spain's Banco de Bilbao and an estate agent's office in the French Basque region in the early 1990s.
The attacks were claimed by the French Basque separatist group Iparetarak (Those of the North).
